videos.title: Structure of a Neuron
videos.watchFor: Connect each neuron structure to the direction of information flow.

videos.title: Action Potential in the Neuron
videos.watchFor: Pause at each graph phase and name the open channel, moving ion, and voltage direction.

videos.title: Synaptic Transmission
videos.watchFor: Follow the sequence from arriving action potential to postsynaptic response.

videos.title: Peripheral Nervous System
videos.watchFor: Organize somatic and autonomic pathways beneath the PNS.

videos.title: The Human Brain: Major Structures and Functions
videos.watchFor: Identify how named regions work as connected networks.

videos.title: The Nervous System, Part 1
videos.watchFor: Separate sensory input, central processing, and motor output, then connect that pathway to the unit's neuron and sensory evidence.

videos.title: Vision
videos.watchFor: Separate optical focusing, retinal transduction, and brain processing.

videos.title: Hearing and Balance
videos.watchFor: Track the change from pressure wave to mechanical vibration to hair-cell signalling.

videos.title: Endocrine System, Part 1
videos.watchFor: Compare hormone transport and target-cell response with neural signalling.

videos.title: The Anterior Pituitary
videos.watchFor: Trace one releasing hormone, pituitary hormone, target gland, and feedback signal.

videos.title: The Pituitary Gland
videos.watchFor: Separate hypothalamic control, anterior-pituitary secretion, and posterior-pituitary release.

videos.title: Thyroid Gland and Thyroid Problems
videos.watchFor: Trace TRH, TSH, thyroid hormone, targets, and feedback separately.

videos.title: Insulin and Glucagon
videos.watchFor: Compare the high-glucose and low-glucose branches, then identify which target is tissue-specific.

videos.title: How Stress Affects Your Body
videos.watchFor: Compare short-term adaptive responses with evidence from prolonged stress.

imageAlt: Comparison of an unmyelinated axon with continuous conduction and a myelinated axon with action potentials regenerated at nodes of Ranvier.
accessibility.textEquivalent: Read the figure: Myelin covers the spaces between nodes. Local current spreads under the myelin, and the full action potential is regenerated at each node. The impulse does not literally leap through empty space.

imageAlt: A receptor sends information through a sensory neuron to interneurons in the spinal cord, followed by a motor neuron leading to a muscle.
accessibility.textEquivalent: Read the figure: Neuron type is defined by its role and direction of information, not by one universal cell shape. A reflex pathway can produce a rapid spinal response while information also travels to the brain.

imageAlt: A neuron membrane at rest with more sodium outside, more potassium inside, potassium leak channels, and a sodium-potassium pump moving three sodium ions out and two potassium ions in.
accessibility.textEquivalent: Read the figure: Ion gradients, selective permeability, and the sodium-potassium pump support a resting voltage near −70 mV. The pump maintains the gradients; it does not cause each action-potential phase by itself.
